title: Give StartDateWindowException a stable error code instead of a raw pre-formatted English message (EH-5)

evidence.quote: 'Program start date cannot be in the future. '

why: EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry stable codes/enums rather than pre-formatted human messages, specifically because this is an EN+Hebrew app where a raw English string renders untranslated for Hebrew-locale users. StartDateWindowException (thrown from the live B2/B3 date-window invariant, reached via ProgramStartingPosition.fromLegacyGrammar → track_blueprint.dart) is constructed with a fully-formatted English sentence, and it extends AppException whose only payload field is `final String message` — there is no code/enum to key an ARB lookup off. A repo-wide grep found no catch site for StartDateWindowException anywhere in lib/, so if the 30-day window is ever violated by legacy/migrated data (not just live UI input, which the picker constrains), the raw English text is the only representation available to whatever eventually surfaces it to the user.
recommendation: Add a stable code/enum to StartDateWindowException (or to the AppException hierarchy generally) and have the presentation layer resolve it via AppLocalizations instead of displaying `message` directly.
acceptance_criteria: StartDateWindowException exposes a stable, locale-independent identifier (enum/const code) alongside or instead of the free-text message.
Any UI that surfaces this exception resolves the user-facing string via AppLocalizations/ARB, verified by an EN+HE widget test.

corrections: app_exception.dart quote is at line 35, not 33. TrackBlueprint.fromLegacyResult (the only path to this exception) has zero lib/ callers — only its own test invokes it; the claimed exposure path is currently dead code, not a live risk.

app_exception.dart citation says line 33 but 'final String message;' is actually at line 35 (line 33 is blank) — 2-line offset, quote text itself is real and correctly found nearby; doesn't change the finding's validity.
